Alex P.: quick heads-up: onboarding report — a few customers hit TS errors on edge when using our JS SDK with generics.
Sam K.: what import form are they using? default vs named?
Alex P.: default import: `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` then `Redwood.createClient<MyTypes>({})`. local tsc OK, Vercel Edge build fails: "No overload matches this call".
June C.: classic. Overlapping overloads + generic default = brittle across moduleResolution modes.
June C.: short fixes: 1) prefer named export for createClient types (export function createClient...) and export default the symbol for runtime; 2) tighten generic defaults to `T extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, unknown>`.
Sam K.: also add conditional `types` in package.exports so ESM consumers pick the matching d.ts (publish dist/types/esm and dist/types/cjs).
Alex P.: for quickstart README, suggest `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` for edge and include tsconfig snippet: `{ "compilerOptions": { "moduleResolution": "bundler", "esModuleInterop": true } }`.
doc-bot: created issue #1401: "sdk: edge typing - overloads & tsconfig guidance"
Alex P.: I'll send a tiny PR: change overloads to avoid overlap, named exports + default delegator, conditional types, and add CI consumer tsc check. ETA tomorrow.
Sam K.: :+1: include a tiny repro consumer that runs `tsc` with nodeNext and bundler to catch regressions.
June C.: happy to review emitted d.ts.
